page.layout: One page of verse, one column of italic lines under a running head; no margin notes; a small mark at the foot left.

p.i: Qui dextera rubente solus torqueat Flammas,& horridos trisulci fulminis Tonans fragores mittat athere, & truci Verberet agrestium labores grandine: Nec impotentes me procellas Siribus Meis per aquor excitare concitum, Piceósque turbines per arua, ni prius Annuerit ipse magnus Omnium arbiter. Et dira me licet malignitas agat Per turpe quoduis precipitem scelus, tamen Scio paratam caetibus Sitam bonis, Auferre quam non Silla possint tempora: Scio paratam caetibus mortem malis, Nullisque finianda seclis termina.

Sed terra plurimos suo sinu fouet Vbique mortales, quibus meis dolis Mens fascinata pluribus manult Deis Seruire, quos dolauit artificum manus, Quam reddere Sni Sota pura Numini. Et sunt furor quos tantus occupat, Deum Vt esse pernegent: & illa cuncta censeant Ridenda Sani cordis esse somnia, Qua fabricasse machinam immensi docent Orbis potente Calites nutu: & regi Mundum ambigua non fortis impetu Sago, Sed mentis aeterna sacratis legibus.
Quid? punicendis nulla culpis Tartara, Crucesque nullas esse post fatum putant, Nec Sika pias manere turbas pramia.

page.notes: Printed text is set in italic throughout. Several words in the Greek-like or Latin-like forms (e.g. "Siribus", "Sitam", "Sni", "Sota", "Sago", "Sika") are doubtful readings of heavily worn capitals and may be misread. The small mark at the lower left is a stain, not transcribed. A printed figure in the right margin (a partial "H" mark) is a stray stain.
